title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 76-79): Grothendieck is setting up a general 'structure at infinity' formalism for a complex analytic space X with a divisor Θ (ultimately X = the Deligne-Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}, with Θ its boundary divisor). The setup is as follows.

- X is stratified by depth: D_d is the locus where at least d branches of the divisor meet. Chains d_* = (d_0 > ... > d_r) index the spaces D_{d_*}. These spaces form a simplicial-type system whose degeneracy operators are isomorphisms. The previous page normalizes the notation (indices strictly decreasing, last index > 0 unless r = 0) and adds the projections D_{d_*} → D_0 = X.
- D^*_{d_*} denotes the open stratum, i.e. D_{d_*} minus the deeper strata.
- V_{d_*} denotes germs of tubular neighbourhoods of strata, and V^*_{d_*} the same neighbourhoods with the deeper divisor removed.
- The V_{d_*,d'_*} and V^*_{d_*,d'_*} are the 'building pieces' (pièces de construction) from which the open variety X \ Θ, and the whole topological type, is to be reassembled.

On this page he works out the most elementary example (261): X = the analytic affine line, Θ = {0}.

Non-empty index chains: {0}, {1}, {1,0}. Non-trivial inclusions: {0}→{0,1} and {1}→{0,1}. The spaces are:
- D_0 = C, D_0^* = C^*.
- D_1 = D_1^* = {P}, the origin.
- D_{1,0} ≅ D_1, with D_{1,0}^* = D_{1,0} and structure map D_{1,0} → D_0 the inclusion of {0} into C.
- V_0^* ≅ V_0 ≅ D_0^* = C^*, a trivial fibration with point fibres.
- V_1 = the germ of open discs centred at 0.
- V_1^* = the germ of punctured discs.
- V_{1,0} ≅ V_1 and V_{1,0}^* ≅ V_1^*.

Conclusion, finished on the next page: four building pieces, two global (C^*, the pointed P) and two local (the disc germ D, the punctured disc germ D^*). They assemble along the diagram D^* ↪ D, D^* → C^*, P → D, and C is recovered as the pushout C ≅ C^* ∐_{D^*} D.

In modern terms, this is the toy case of describing a space with a normal-crossings boundary as a (homotopy) colimit of strata and their deleted tubular neighbourhoods, indexed by the poset of strata.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equalities D_1 = D_1^* and D_{1,0} ≅ D_1 are consistent with the normalization conventions of p.77.
The 'trivial fibration' V_0 → D_0^* (point fibres) is a degenerate convention: the depth-0 'tubular neighbourhood' is the open stratum itself. This is fine but purely formal.

ideas.what: Decomposition of a variety with divisor into strata indexed by chains of depths, with tubular and punctured tubular neighbourhood germs as building pieces, recovering the space by gluing
ideas.modern_name: Stratified spaces with control data / tubular neighbourhood systems; deleted neighbourhoods; homotopy colimit over the strata poset (exit-path / link decomposition); compare Kato-Nakayama real blow-up
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (1970s); Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, 1988); Kato-Nakayama (1999); Lurie/Treumann (exit paths)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} and to 'tame' (modérée) topology, but not to this explicit formalism

ideas.what: Elementary example: C with divisor {0} gives pieces C^*, point, disc germ, punctured disc germ, with C = C^* ∐_{D^*} D
ideas.modern_name: Van Kampen-type gluing / tubular-neighbourhood decomposition of a curve near a puncture

deep.surprise_reason: The page only works out the trivial one-point example of a general stratification and tubular-neighbourhood formalism. The general framework belongs to the surrounding pages, and its ideas parallel well-known Thom-Mather and log-geometric constructions. Nothing on this page is new.
transcription_corrections: 'X = E^{1 an}': the analytic affine line, i.e. C.

The crossed-out block under 'On aura' was abandoned: D_1 = D_1^* ≃ D_{1,0} = D_{1,0}^* = origine de C, and V_1 = V_0, C. The margin note about (262)/(263) concerns dropping a trailing index 0, i.e. D_{d,0} ≅ D_d.
'{+germe+} [-disque-] de disques ouverts centrés en 0' is correct: the germ of open discs centred at 0.
The struck-out top-left margin note refers to the building pieces V_{d_*,d'_*}, V^*_{d_*,d'_*} and the maps φ_{d_*,d'_*}, cross-referenced to (260).
